slot.brief: A person standing on a lift accelerating upward/downward; ask the apparent weight as a multiple of true weight using N = m(g ± a).

stem: A passenger stands on a weighing scale in a lift accelerating vertically upward at $3\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. Taking $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, the apparent weight is what multiple of the passenger’s true weight?

verdicts.working: For upward acceleration, apparent weight is N = m(g + a) = 13m; true weight is mg = 10m. Their ratio is 1.3.

working:
$N-mg=ma \Rightarrow N=m(g+a)$
$\dfrac{N}{mg}=\dfrac{g+a}{g}=\dfrac{10+3}{10}=1.3$
